_purpose: Per-engine surviving-mutant budgets for audit_mutation.py. A surviving mutant is a finding NO fixture can distinguish from a finding that was never emitted: the gate may be correct, but nothing proves it is and nothing would notice if a future edit broke it.
_policy: A BUDGET IS A DEBT, NEVER AN ALLOWANCE. The only legitimate edit to a number here is a DECREASE. Raising one to make a release pass is the exact move this file exists to make visible — it converts 'we added an untested finding' from an invisible event into a reviewable diff. A new gate ships with fixtures that kill its own mutants, or it does not ship (spec §21).
_why_this_file_exists: GAP-2026-08-16-STEP5-SESSION-EXHAUSTION, deployment review. Release 2026.08.15.9 added five gates — C10, C11, MS-12, MS-13, SPEC-BUDGET — and every one of them survived deletion with CI fully green. audit_mutation reported 35/35 killed, 100%, straight through that release, because ENGINE_DEFAULT was audit_canonical.py (the EXAM auditor) and the REPO auditors were outside its universe entirely. The tool was working perfectly on a target that did not include the thing that broke. One global number would have let a new untested finding hide inside the estate's inherited debt, so the budget is per engine.
_measured: 2026-08-16, releases .11 and .12. Verified serial==parallel on mock_sync_audit. NOTE: --jobs helps ONLY on a multi-core runner; see _runner_note.

_survivor_inventory._note: audit_mutation.py gained its own --self-test in B7 and validate.yml now runs it as a blocking step BEFORE the gates it guards. It had none — the one tool whose entire job is proving other tests are connected. The cost was measured: the scaffolding exclusion tested only the INNERMOST enclosing function, so a `sorted(` inside a NESTED test helper's DOCSTRING was listed as a live target and counted as a surviving mutant of the production engine. A false target is not harmless — it puts a phantom in a file whose whole value is that its numbers are real debt. All six are INHERITED, pre-dating this release. None belongs to a gate added by 2026.08.15.9 or .10: C10, C11, MS-12, MS-13 and SPEC-BUDGET are all killed.
analyse_engine.py: B7 killed 19 of the 20. Nine of them lived in FIVE FUNCTIONS THE SUITE HAD NEVER CALLED — synthesise_subtopic, compute_section_axis_distribution, write_section_rules, write_subtopic_manifest, rebuild_subtopic_manifest_from_section_rules. The blocker was mechanical, not editorial: each writes to a hardcoded '/mnt/user-data/outputs/', absent on a CI runner, so no fixture COULD call them. An additive out_dir=None (default unchanged; no production call site touched, no artefact moved) removed it — the same remedy search_dirs applied after GAP-2026-08-17-B4-ENV-SKEW.

The fixture is a new SHAPE: a small corpus driven end to end, assertions reading the emitted artefacts back. Adversarial by construction — 4 sections colliding on one prefix out of alphabetical order (1 in 24), 4 papers with all-different figural counts so the per-paper series is a permutation detector (1 in 24), 4 years whose set order is not their sorted order. A fixture whose values are all equal cannot see an ordering defect; that is how nine survived a suite of 86 checks.
TWO REAL DEFECTS FELL OUT OF THE MEASUREMENT, which is the argument for the gate's runtime:

D7 — subtopic_option_format used q.get('year','?'), putting a str into a dict of int keys that the next line sorts. ONE year-less question raised TypeError inside synthesise_subtopic, which runs for EVERY subtopic: a hard stop of Step 5, invisible on the reference corpus because every IIT_JAM_MATHEMATICS question carries a year. The same sentinel made that function's own no-years guard unreachable — which is why its mutant survived while a fixture NAMED for that branch passed. Both facts were true at once and only one reading explains both: the fixture never reached the line it was named after.

QV-13 was HALF A GATE — it re-derived form_key to detect drift and discarded the freshly-derived collision_domain, though identity is the PAIR and the uniqueness test buckets by that pair. B6 pinned mint_subtopic_ids and stamp_mechanic_axes; the GATE that notices when they drift was not pinned. Found because the mutant that hash-orders its prefix map SURVIVED: nothing downstream read the result. Now both halves are compared, with the same curator-override escape hatch.

The five 'error message' survivors were NOT written off as equivalent. Each enumerates a SET inside a hard stop, so the same corrupt overrides file refuses in different words on every run — a curator cannot diff two runs or grep for a known message. D4 applies to what the operator READS, not only to what the writers EMIT. Each is now asserted verbatim with >=3 members.

1 SURVIVES, PROVEN EQUIVALENT, documented at its own site: _compute_structural_changes `years_seen = sorted(set(...))`. It is read on four lines and every one is order-invariant — truthiness, max(), min(), len(). No fixture can kill it, so none is faked; the sorted() stays so that the day an order-dependent read is added the ordering is already right. If that day comes, the comment at the site is the thing to delete and the mutant becomes killable.
STANDING RULE MET for this engine: every survivor is either killed or PROVEN equivalent.

_usage: python3 audit_mutation.py --engine audit_specs_ext.py --jobs 8   # exits 1 above budget
python3 audit_mutation.py --engine audit_sync.py --shard 3/14 --jobs 1   # one bounded slice
# A SHARDED RUN NEVER ENFORCES A BUDGET — a fraction of the survivors cannot be
# compared against a whole-engine number; audit_mutation suppresses it and says so.
_runner_note: CORRECTION TO .11. That release documented --jobs as the remedy for audit_sync's ~30-minute run. Measured on the reference container: nproc = 1. The mutants are CPU-bound subprocesses, so on a single core parallelism buys nothing and adds contention — 7 mutants at --jobs 7 did not finish in 240 s, while ONE mutant at --jobs 1 took 140 s (63 s baseline + 63 s mutant + copy). --jobs is still correct on a multi-core CI runner and is where the 30 min -> 4 min claim comes from; it is not a universal remedy and .11 should not have written it as one. On a single core, use --shard.

audit_sync.py.why_no_budget_yet: 3 survivors in the first 5 emissions is real evidence of a coverage gap and is NOT an estimate of the whole. A budget derived by extrapolation would assert a number nobody measured, which is precisely the defect class this tool exists to catch. The key stays out of `engines` — report-only — until a full run supplies a real total.
audit_sync.py.what_the_survivors_mean: Each is a finding no fixture can distinguish from silence. The two SKILL-INVENTORY ones are notable: SKILL.md's declared counts are exactly the kind of hand-written number this corpus has watched drift before, and nothing currently proves the check that guards them still fires.
audit_sync.py.finish_it:
python3 audit_mutation.py --engine audit_sync.py --jobs 8
# or, one at a time, on a constrained runner:
python3 audit_mutation.py --engine audit_sync.py --indices 9
python3 audit_mutation.py --engine audit_sync.py --list   # index map
audit_sync.py.measurement_cost: ~63 s per self-test on a 1-core runner, so ~126 s per mutant plus a 63 s baseline per invocation. The reference container's command wall is ~250 s, which admits ONE mutant per call — 19 calls for the remainder. On a multi-core CI box the whole engine is one ~4-minute command.
audit_sync.py.pattern_so_far: 5 survivors in 9 emissions. Every one is an ERROR-PATH or DECLARED-COUNT finding: an unreadable file, an invalid JSON, a trigger SKILL.md forgot, a hand-written count. The fixtures exercise the HAPPY corpus thoroughly and the degraded corpus hardly at all — which is the shape worth knowing even before the remaining 19 are measured, because it says what the missing fixtures should DO rather than merely how many are missing.

_pipeline_kind: audit_mutation gained a second mutation model in Wave 2 Part C B4. It was built for AUDITORS — it neutralises a FINDING EMISSION and asks whether a fixture notices. Pointed at analyse_engine.py (4,847 lines of Step 5 pipeline) it reported '0 emission(s)', because a pipeline computes values rather than emitting findings. The corpus's largest new engine therefore sat OUTSIDE the gate while CI reported 100% — the exact shape _why_this_file_exists already describes: 'The tool was working perfectly on a target that did not include the thing that broke.' --kind pipeline mutates DECISION POINTS instead, and kind is auto-detected so an engine with zero targets now EXITS 1 rather than banking a vacuous 100%.
